title: Platform systems & services playbook, runbooks, dashboards and roadmap (Q3 2026)
author: Lena Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This page is the canonical Platform Systems & Services playbook for Redwood Inference. It consolidates the systems inventory, operational runbooks, dashboard and alerting standards, common how-tos, retrospective notes from recent incidents, and the near-term roadmap (Q3 2026). Use this document as the first stop for platform oncall, engineers onboarding to platform services, and cross-team coordination.

1) Scope & goals
-----------------
- Scope: core platform services that support inference runtime, orchestration, networking, capacity management, and developer-facing platform tooling. Includes services listed in the inventory below.
- Goals:
  - Maintain platform SLOs (availability, p99/p50 latency) and clear oncall runbooks.
  - Provide standardized dashboards and alert rules to reduce noise and mean time to resolution (MTTR).
  - Align roadmap items to reliability and cost-efficiency priorities (batching, KV cache improvements, autoscaling).

2) Systems & services inventory (high level)
-------------------------------------------
Service | Owner | Primary channel | Runbook
-------|-------|-----------------|--------
router-api | eng-platform-router (team: platform) | #platform-router | /runbooks/router-api-runbook
inference-gateway | eng-serving-runtime | #inference-gateway | /runbooks/inference-gateway
kv-cache | eng-serving-runtime | #kv-cache | /runbooks/kv-cache
batcher | eng-platform-batching | #batcher | /runbooks/batcher
model-store | eng-platform-storage | #model-store | /runbooks/model-store
metrics-agent | eng-platform-monitoring | #platform-monitoring | /runbooks/metrics-agent
capacity-manager | eng-sre | #capacity | /runbooks/capacity-manager

(Ownership above is the system-level owner. For feature-level questions see respective product PRD pages.)

3) Standard platform SLOs & key metrics
---------------------------------------
- Availability (global, all services): 99.95% monthly (error budget 0.05%).
- Inference request latency (p99): <= 150 ms for small models (seq len <= 512) on dedicated capacity; p50 <= 20 ms.
- API success rate: >= 99.9% (5xx rate < 0.1%).
- Controller reconciliation time (k8s controllers): p95 < 30s.
- Model load time (cold): < 120s (target for major models).

Key metrics to show on dashboards: request_rate, error_rate (5xx/4xx), p50/p95/p99 latencies, queue_depth (batcher), kv_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_utilization, reclaimable_memory, pod_restarts, reconciliation_latency, model_load_duration.

4) Dashboards & alerting standards (how we design panels & alerts)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Design principles:
- One-pane-of-glass per service: each service dashboard includes traffic, errors, latency histograms, infra health (CPU/GPU/memory), and recent deploys.
- Use SLO-based alerts first (burn-rate alerts) and instrumentation-level alerts second.
- Keep page-to-oncall relationship explicit in alert definitions.

Recommended Grafana panels (examples with PromQL where relevant):
- Panel: router-api latency (p99)
  - Query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="router-api"}[5m])))
- Panel: inference-gateway p50/p95/p99
  - Queries: histogram_quantile(0.50, ...), histogram_quantile(0.95, ...), histogram_quantile(0.99, ...)
- Panel: kv_cache hit ratio
  - Query: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- Panel: GPU utilization (per node)
  - Query: avg by (instance) (nvidia_gpu_utilization_percentage)

Standard alert rules (Prometheus-style, with SLO/burn-rate where applicable):
1) Alert: PlatformHighErrorRate
   - Scope: any production service with errors > 0.5% for 3m AND >1% for 15m
   - Severity: P1
   - Pager: oncall-platform primary; escalate to eng-sre after 10m if not acknowledged
   - Runbook: follow service-specific error investigation (see Runbooks section)

2) Alert: InferenceP99LatencyDegradation
   - Scope: inference-gateway p99 > 2x baseline for 5m OR > 200ms for 10m
   - Severity: P1 for dedicated customers, P2 for non-dedicated
   - Pager: oncall-inference -> eng-platform-router if routing errors detected

3) Alert: KVCacheLowHitRatio
   - Scope: kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m
   - Severity: P2
   - Action: inspect recent cache evictions, model-serving traffic patterns; consider TTL configuration rollback

4) Alert: GPUNodeUnhealthy
   - Scope: any GPU node not Ready OR nvidia driver errors OR gpu_utilization == 0 but pods pending for > 2m
   - Severity: P1
   - Action: check node events, restart kubelet, cordon & drain if hardware suspected

Alert routing and escalation table:
- P0/P1 -> immediate PagerDuty page to oncall (platform or serving runtime based on service)
- P2 -> Slack alert to team channel and create ticket in Jira with predefined template

5) Runbooks (operational playbooks for common incidents)
------------------------------------------------------
A. Runbook: router-api high error rate (PlatformHighErrorRate)
1. Check the dashboard: traffic, error rate, recent deploys.
2. Identify first failure time and correlate with deploys: `kubectl get deploy -o wide --selector=app=router-api --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp` and check build tags.
3. If 5xx spikes and pods show OOMKilled or CrashLoopBackOff, collect pod logs: `kubectl logs -n prod <pod> --previous` and examine stack traces.
4. If traffic pattern spike (e.g., misbehaving client), temporarily apply rate-limiting rule: `kubectl apply -f k8s/ratelimit-temporary.yaml` and contact the client.
5. If a config rollout caused regression, rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/router-api` and monitor.
6. After mitigation, create post-incident ticket and link retrospective template.

B. Runbook: inference-gateway p99 latency spike
1. Verify model-serving nodes and KV cache hit ratio.
2. Check batching queue depth: `sum(rate(batcher_queue_length[1m])) by (model)`; if queue growing, consider increasing batch worker counts or temporary quota adjustments.
3. If GPU saturation detected, check autoscaler logs and capacity-manager; scale up reserved nodes if capacity_manager.policy == "reserved"; otherwise route traffic to fallback model variant.
4. If kernel-level slowdowns (known regression), escalate to eng-serving-runtime with trace bundle (collect perf profile, nvprof output if applicable).

C. Runbook: GPU node failure
1. Cordon the node: `kubectl cordon <node>`
2. Drain non-critical pods: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3. Check driver and kernel logs (`/var/log/nvidia-driver.log`, `dmesg`), restart kubelet if transient.
4. Engage infra (oncall infra) if hardware replacement needed; open Hardware RMA ticket with vendor and attach node diagnostics.

6) Common how-tos (short how-to recipes)
---------------------------------------
- How to add a new Grafana panel:
  1. Duplicate the service dashboard.
  2. Add panel with PromQL query and set legend & unit.
  3. Add panel threshold aligned to SLO and save to `team-dashboards` folder.
- How to add an alert:
  1. Create rule in prometheus/ruler namespace `platform-rules`.
  2. Set annotations: summary, runbook, pagerduty-service.
  3. Link to service runbook and test with `promtool test rules` in staging.
- How to add oncall rotation: update `oncall-schedule.yaml` in infra repo and run the infra CI job to apply.

7) Recent postmortem highlights & retrospectives (last 6 months)
---------------------------------------------------------------
Incident: Model-loading NPE causing p50 latency regression (2025-12-07)
- Root cause: a model-descriptor edge case for models with empty tokenizer metadata.
- Action items: add defensive checks in model loader (PR #4521), add unit tests for descriptor parsing, add synthetic e2e test to catch cold load regressions.
- Status: completed and deployment rolled out 2026-01-10.

Incident: Batcher queue amplification during A/B experiment (2026-01-28)
- Root cause: misconfigured traffic weights in router-api led to concentrated burst on heavyweight model variant.
- Action items: add circuit-breaker at router layer, add deployment guardrails and traffic sanity check pre-deploy.
- Status: guardrail implemented 2026-02-05.

8) Q3 2026 roadmap (platform priorities)
----------------------------------------
- Reliability: KV cache eviction policy improvements and adaptive TTLs (owner: eng-serving-runtime) - target: reduce cold load rate by 30%.
- Cost: batching optimizer 2.0 (owner: eng-platform-batching) - prioritized for 10-20% token-cost reduction on high-throughput workloads.
- Observability: unified SLO dashboard and burn-rate automation (owner: eng-platform-monitoring) - target: reduce noise by 40%.
- Onboarding: platform runbook templates and one-click dashboard creation for new services (owner: eng-platform) - target: onboard 5 teams in Q3

Milestones and dates:
- May 2026: finished KV cache TTL prototype (experimental)
- Jul 2026: rollout batching optimizer to staging
- Aug 2026: unify SLO dashboard and alert tuning (phase 1)
- Sep 2026: platform-runbook templating v1 and team onboarding pilot

9) Team wiki & useful links
---------------------------
- Platform team wiki (living docs): /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki
- Runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks-index
- Dashboard folder: Grafana -> Redwood/Platform -> Service Dashboards
- Alert rules repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/platform-alerts
- Oncall schedules & PagerDuty: /confluence/eng-platform/oncall

10) Ownership, oncall and escalation matrix
-------------------------------------------
Service owners are responsible for dashboards, runbooks, and SLO targets. Oncall rotation is 1 week primary, 1 week secondary. Escalation path:
- Primary oncall (service team) -> Secondary oncall (platform) after 10 minutes -> Eng-SRE after 20 minutes -> Engineering Director if unresolved > 2 hours.

11) Appendix: alert thresholds quick reference (table)
----------------------------------------------------
Alert Name | Trigger | Severity | Pager
-----------|---------|----------|------
PlatformHighErrorRate | errors > 0.5% for 3m & >1% for 15m | P1 | oncall-platform
InferenceP99LatencyDegradation | p99 > 200ms for 10m | P1 (dedicated) / P2 (hosted) | oncall-inference
KVCacheLowHitRatio | hit_ratio < 0.6 for 10m | P2 | eng-serving-runtime
GPUNodeUnhealthy | node NotReady OR driver errors | P1 | infra-oncall

12) Maintenance & review cadence
--------------------------------
- Dashboard and alert review: monthly (first Monday) - owners must validate noise and thresholds.
- Runbook review: quarterly - owners update steps and commands.
- Roadmap sync: bi-weekly with eng-sre and product managers.

If you are new to platform oncall: follow the Oncall Quickstart (link on wiki) and shadow a senior oncall for two rotations before taking primary.

Feedback / updates: file PRs against this page or ping the page owner in #platform-docs.
